principles: Pre-reg rev3.1 is the authority — enumeration, applicability, schema and denominator rules mirror §1/§3/§5/§7 exactly.
Separate orchestration from execution: the driver owns the matrix + record canonicalization; the per-cell engine is injected so the core is deterministic and offline-testable.
Reuse, do not re-implement: adjudicate.mjs for outcome, checks.mjs for the three pass-flags + unsafe detectors, run-recovery.mjs as the real engine.
Every emitted record self-describes its denominator-set membership so downstream rates always have a published denominator.
Fail-closed validity filter: only harness/infra failure voids+re-runs; task-level failures are real outcomes kept.
drivers: Must match the pre-registered §7 21-field schema and §3 applicability matrix verbatim.
Selfcheck must run with zero live-model calls (offline, deterministic) yet exercise the same record-assembly path the real campaign uses.
Must not modify adjudicate/checks/run-recovery behavior nor run the powered campaign in this story.

options.name: injected-engine-driver
pros: Driver core (enumeration/applicability/denominator/canonicalization/validity/seeded-order) unit-tested with a deterministic stub engine — no claude -p
Real campaign plugs run-recovery as the engine unchanged
Clean separation, each unit independently testable
cons: One extra indirection layer (engine interface) to define

options.name: extend-run-ablation-inline
pros: No new file; reuse existing arm->runner mapping
cons: run-ablation already spawns claude -p so its core cannot be offline-tested without heavy refactor
Mixes enumeration with live execution — violates the deterministic/offline requirement
Larger blast radius on a file used by other flows

rationale: The pre-reg demands a deterministic, offline-testable harness validated before the multi-day compute campaign. Injecting the per-cell engine lets the driver core be fully exercised by a stub (no live model) while the real run plugs run-recovery unchanged; extending run-ablation inline cannot meet the offline-test requirement because it already shells out to claude -p. UNKNOWN-1 resolved: pre-register 4 contrasts and stamp denominatorSets[] = every contrast whose common-cell set contains the run, where membership = (run.arm is one of the two contrast arms) AND (run.scenarioId applies to BOTH arms): A4_vs_A2prime (PRIMARY, H1/H2; all scenarios+null), A4_vs_A3 (EXPLORATORY, H3), A4_vs_A2 (reference), A4_vs_A1 (reference; excludes B4/B5/B10 which are N/A for A1). UNKNOWN-2 resolved: add experiments/recovery-runner/run-selfchecks.mjs aggregator (runs adjudicate+checks+spend-accounting+run-driver selfchecks) + a root npm `test:experiments` script appended to the root test chain — this both satisfies the checklist promise and retroactively wires the three pre-existing experiment selfchecks that were previously standalone.

preMortem.scenario: Enumeration miscounts because applicability is applied per-arm wrong
preMortem.trigger: B4/B5/B10 emitted for A1, or the 12 universal scenarios dropped from some arm
preMortem.consequence: Cell matrix wrong -> denominators wrong -> every downstream rate biased
preMortem.mitigation: Selfcheck asserts exact per-arm scenario sets and total cell count against a hand-computed expected value; N/A exclusions logged

preMortem.scenario: Emitted record drifts from the §7 schema (missing/renamed field)
preMortem.trigger: Hand-built record object instead of a single canonicalizer
preMortem.consequence: Analysis script + GLMM break or silently misread fields
preMortem.mitigation: Single buildCanonicalRecord() with an explicit 21-field allowlist; selfcheck asserts every record has exactly those keys and adjudicatedOutcome in the §7 enum

preMortem.scenario: Validity filter drops a real task-level failure as infra-void
preMortem.trigger: Confusing a model task-failure with a harness/API outage
preMortem.mitigation: Void only on an explicit infra-failure signal from the engine result; selfcheck proves task-failure kept and only infra-failure triggers re-run+log

preMortem.scenario: Editing root package.json test chain breaks unrelated tests or trips scope/boundary gates
preMortem.trigger: test:experiments added incorrectly or a selfcheck is slow/flaky
preMortem.consequence: npm test red -> done_required fails; or REVIEW scope friction
preMortem.mitigation: Aggregator runs only fast offline node selfchecks; verify full npm test green before REVIEW; package.json edit is within the user-confirmed scope boundary
